message: No detected input validation: No schema checks, dtype assertions, or value-range guards are visible in the data-acquisition path; data is passed directly into pipelines without validation.
No detected untrusted source handling: Data is fetched from IBM COS and Cloudant without any checksum verification, signed-URL validation, or pinned revision checks.
No detected label flipping detection: No code checks label distributions, validates label values against an expected set, or uses any label-noise detection tool before training.
No detected data poisoning defenses: No outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or filtering of suspicious training samples is present in any of the code slices shown.

No detected model integrity verification: The model is loaded via pickle from a COS bucket and a local checkpoint file without any hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision to verify integrity.
No detected label distribution validation: No code validates label distribution, class balance, or expected label sets before or during training.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no neural-cleanse, activation analysis, gradient anomaly detection, or any other backdoor defense in the training code.
No detected differential privacy: No differential privacy library (Opacus, TensorFlow Privacy, DP-SGD) or related mechanism is imported or used anywhere in the code.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: There is no use of Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD, or any other adversarial attack/robustness testing framework anywhere in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: There is no evidence of a held-out test set isolated from training, signed/hashed evaluation data, or multiple independent metrics being enforced to protect against metric manipulation.
No detected input sanitization: The predict_pipeline function directly transforms and passes data to the model without any shape, range, type, or schema validation on incoming request data.
No detected output bounds checks: The inference code returns model.predict(X_pred).tolist() directly with no NaN guards, probability bounds checks, or threshold validation on the outputs.

No detected prompt injection defenses: Although IBM Watson NLU is used for text sentiment analysis, there is no prompt-injection filtering, system-prompt isolation, or output content moderation implemented in the inference path.
